theory.intro: For a curve given parametrically, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is the gradient of the tangent at that value of $t$, provided $\dfrac{dx}{dt}\neq 0$. Use the parametric derivatives to write tangents and normals, and to find stationary points.
facts: The point on the curve at $t=p$ is $\left(x(p),\,y(p)\right)$, found by substituting $p$ into both equations.
When $\dfrac{dx}{dt}\neq 0$, the tangent at $t=p$ has gradient $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}$ evaluated at $t=p$.

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent. For a finite, nonzero tangent gradient $m$, the normal gradient is $-\dfrac{1}{m}$. A horizontal tangent has a vertical normal, and a vertical tangent has a horizontal normal.
Use $y-y_{1}=m(x-x_{1})$ with the point on the curve, never with the value of $t$.
A stationary point occurs where $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=0$ and $\dfrac{dx}{dt}\neq 0$.
The tangent is vertical where $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=0$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt}\neq 0$.
When a point is given by its coordinates, find $t$ by solving both equations and keeping the common value.
steps: Find the value of $t$ the question needs, and the point $(x,y)$ there.
Write a line with finite gradient using $y-y_{1}=m(x-x_{1})$. Write a vertical line as $x=x_{1}$ and a horizontal line as $y=y_{1}$.

workedExamples.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=t^2$ and $y=6t$. Find the equation of the tangent at $t=3$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
At $t=3$, the point is $(9,18)$.
$\begin{align*}\frac{dx}{dt}&=2t,&\frac{dy}{dt}&=6\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{6}{2t}\\&=\frac{3}{t}\end{align*}$
At $t=3$, the tangent gradient is $1$.
$\begin{align*}y-18&=x-9\\y&=x+9\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=2t^2$ and $y=6t$. Find the equation of the normal at $t=3$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
At $t=3$, the point is $(18,18)$.
$\begin{align*}\frac{dx}{dt}&=4t,&\frac{dy}{dt}&=6\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{6}{4t}\\&=\frac{3}{2t}\end{align*}$
At $t=3$, the tangent gradient is $\frac12$, so the normal gradient is $-2$.
$\begin{align*}y-18&=-2(x-18)\\y&=-2x+54\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=t^3+t$ and $y=t^2-6t$. Find the coordinates of its stationary point.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\frac{dx}{dt}&=3t^2+1,&\frac{dy}{dt}&=2t-6\end{align*}$
A stationary point requires $\frac{dy}{dt}=0$ and $\frac{dx}{dt}\ne0$.
$\begin{align*}2t-6&=0\\t&=3\end{align*}$
At $t=3$, $\frac{dx}{dt}=28\ne0$.
$\begin{align*}x&=3^3+3=30\\y&=3^2-6(3)=-9\end{align*}$
The stationary point is $(30,-9)$.

workedExamples.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=t^2-6t$ and $y=t^3-3t$. Find the coordinates of the point where its tangent is vertical.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\frac{dx}{dt}&=2t-6,&\frac{dy}{dt}&=3t^2-3\end{align*}$
A vertical tangent requires $\frac{dx}{dt}=0$ and $\frac{dy}{dt}\ne0$.
$\begin{align*}2t-6&=0\\t&=3\end{align*}$
At $t=3$, $\frac{dy}{dt}=24\ne0$.
$\begin{align*}x&=3^2-6(3)=-9\\y&=3^3-3(3)=18\end{align*}$
The tangent is vertical at $(-9,18)$.

workedExamples.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=3t$ and $y=t^3$. Find the coordinates of all points where the tangent has gradient $9$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\frac{dx}{dt}&=3,&\frac{dy}{dt}&=3t^2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{3t^2}{3}\\&=t^2\end{align*}$
For gradient $9$:
$\begin{align*}t^2&=9\\t&=\pm3\end{align*}$
Since $\frac{dx}{dt}=3\ne0$, both values are valid. At $t=3$, the point is $(9,27)$; at $t=-3$, it is $(-9,-27)$.

workedExamples.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=2t^2$ and $y=t^3$. Find the equation of the tangent at $(18,27)$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Find a parameter value satisfying both coordinates.
$\begin{align*}2t^2&=18\\t&=\pm3\end{align*}$
Since $t^3=27$, take $t=3$.
$\begin{align*}\frac{dx}{dt}&=4t,&\frac{dy}{dt}&=3t^2\end{align*}$
At $t=3$:
$\begin{align*}\frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{27}{12}\\&=\frac94\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}y-27&=\frac94(x-18)\\4y-108&=9x-162\\9x-4y-54&=0\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=3t^2$ and $y=6t$. Show that its tangent at $t=p$ has equation $x-py+3p^2=0$ for every real $p$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
At $t=p$, the point is $(3p^2,6p)$.
$\begin{align*}\frac{dx}{dt}&=6t,&\frac{dy}{dt}&=6\end{align*}$
For $p\ne0$, the tangent gradient is $\frac1p$.
$\begin{align*}y-6p&=\frac1p(x-3p^2)\\py-6p^2&=x-3p^2\\x-py+3p^2&=0\end{align*}$
For $p=0$, the point is $(0,0)$, with $\frac{dx}{dt}=0$ and $\frac{dy}{dt}=6\ne0$. Its tangent is therefore $x=0$, which also follows from the stated equation at $p=0$. The equation holds for every real $p$.

workedExamples.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=3t$ and $y=t^2$. The normal at $t=3$ meets the $x$-axis. Find the coordinates of that intersection.
workedExamples.solution_text:
At $t=3$, the point is $(9,9)$.
$\begin{align*}\frac{dx}{dt}&=3,&\frac{dy}{dt}&=2t\end{align*}$
At $t=3$, the tangent gradient is $\frac63=2$, so the normal gradient is $-\frac12$.
$\begin{align*}y-9&=-\frac12(x-9)\\2y-18&=-x+9\\x+2y&=27\end{align*}$
On the $x$-axis, $y=0$, giving $x=27$. The intersection is $(27,0)$.

workedExamples.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=5\cos t$ and $y=5\sin t$. Find the equations of the tangent and normal at $t=\frac{\pi}{2}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
At $t=\frac{\pi}{2}$, the point is $(0,5)$.
$\begin{align*}\frac{dx}{dt}&=-5\sin t,&\frac{dy}{dt}&=5\cos t\end{align*}$
At this parameter value, $\frac{dx}{dt}=-5\ne0$ and $\frac{dy}{dt}=0$. The tangent is horizontal, so its equation is $y=5$. The normal is vertical, so its equation is $x=0$.

workedExamples.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=t^2-t$ and $y=t^3-12t$. Find all points where the tangent is horizontal.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\frac{dx}{dt}&=2t-1,&\frac{dy}{dt}&=3t^2-12\end{align*}$
A horizontal tangent requires $\frac{dy}{dt}=0$ and $\frac{dx}{dt}\ne0$.
$\begin{align*}3t^2-12&=0\\t^2&=4\\t&=\pm2\end{align*}$
At $t=2$, $\frac{dx}{dt}=3\ne0$, and the point is $(2,-16)$. At $t=-2$, $\frac{dx}{dt}=-5\ne0$, and the point is $(6,16)$. Both points have horizontal tangents.

A curve has parametric equations $x=4\cos t$ and $y=4\sin t$.
Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
foundation.solution_text:
At $t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$: $x=0$ and $y=4$.
$\dfrac{dx}{dt}=-4\sin t$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=4\cos t$
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{4\cos t}{-4\sin t}=-\cot t$
At $t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, $\cot t=0$, so the gradient is $0$.
$y=4$

development.question_text:
A curve has parametric equations $x=t^{3}+t$ and $y=t^{2}-4t$.
Find the coordinates of the stationary point on the curve.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dy}{dt}=2t-4$ and $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=3t^{2}+1$
$2t-4=0$
$t=2$
At $t=2$, $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=13\neq 0$, so the tangent is horizontal.
$x=2^{3}+2=10$ and $y=2^{2}-4(2)=-4$
The stationary point is $(10,-4)$.

development.question_text:
A curve has parametric equations $x=e^{t}$ and $y=t^{2}-2t$.
Find the coordinates of the stationary point on the curve.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dy}{dt}=2t-2$ and $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=e^{t}$
$2t-2=0$
$t=1$
At $t=1$, $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=e\neq 0$, so the tangent is horizontal.
$x=e$ and $y=1-2=-1$
The stationary point is $(e,-1)$.

development.question_text:
A curve has parametric equations $x=t^{2}-t$ and $y=t^{3}-3t$.
Find the coordinates of the points where the tangent to the curve is horizontal.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dy}{dt}=3t^{2}-3$ and $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2t-1$
$3t^{2}-3=0$
$t=\pm 1$
At $t=1$, $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=1\neq 0$; at $t=-1$, $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=-3\neq 0$.
At $t=1$: $x=0$ and $y=-2$.
At $t=-1$: $x=2$ and $y=2$.
The tangent is horizontal at $(0,-2)$ and $(2,2)$.

development.question_text:
A curve has parametric equations $x=t^{3}-3t$ and $y=t^{2}+1$.
Find the coordinates of the points where the tangent to the curve is vertical.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dx}{dt}=3t^{2}-3$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=2t$
$3t^{2}-3=0$
$t=\pm 1$
At $t=1$, $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=2\neq 0$; at $t=-1$, $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=-2\neq 0$.
At $t=1$: $x=-2$ and $y=2$.
At $t=-1$: $x=2$ and $y=2$.
The tangent is vertical at $(-2,2)$ and $(2,2)$.

mastery.question_text:
A curve has parametric equations $x=2t^{2}$ and $y=4t$.
Show that the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=p$ has equation $x-py+2p^{2}=0$.
mastery.solution_text:
At $t=p$: $x=2p^{2}$ and $y=4p$.
$\dfrac{dx}{dt}=4t$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=4$
For $p\neq 0$, the tangent gradient is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{4}{4p}=\dfrac{1}{p}$.
$y-4p=\dfrac{1}{p}\left(x-2p^{2}\right)$
$py-4p^{2}=x-2p^{2}$
$x-py+2p^{2}=0$
For $p=0$, the point is $(0,0)$, $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=0$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=4\neq 0$, so the tangent is vertical with equation $x=0$.
Substituting $p=0$ into $x-py+2p^{2}=0$ also gives $x=0$, so the stated equation holds for every real $p$.

mastery.question_text:
A curve has parametric equations $x=t^{2}-4t$ and $y=t^{3}-3t$.
Find the coordinates of the point where the tangent to the curve is vertical.
mastery.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2t-4$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=3t^{2}-3$
$2t-4=0$
$t=2$
At $t=2$, $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=3(4)-3=9\neq 0$, so the tangent is vertical.
$x=4-8=-4$ and $y=8-6=2$
The tangent is vertical at $(-4,2)$.

mastery.question_text:
A curve has parametric equations $x=4t$ and $y=2t^{2}$.
The normal to the curve at the point where $t=1$ meets the $x$-axis.
Find the coordinates of that point.
mastery.solution_text:
At $t=1$: $x=4$ and $y=2$.
$\dfrac{dx}{dt}=4$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=4t=4$
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=1$
Normal gradient $=-1$.
$y-2=-1(x-4)$
$y=-x+6$
Setting $y=0$ gives $x=6$, so the normal meets the $x$-axis at $(6,0)$.
